messages.subject: Domain error: gsl: gamma.c:1138
parts:
Dear group,

The error occurred when I fit a model with two IID random effects. The sample sizes are small, I suspect predictive sampling can't be done. 
Can you help interpreting the error? The codes are attached.

Thanks
dong

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Domain error: gsl: gamma.c:1138
parts:
seems like there is a missprint here, which caused the problems (at
least for me)

15c15
< priot="logtnormal",param=c(0,1e-04)
---
> prior="logtnormal",param=c(0,1e-04)


we do recommend the penalized complexity priors, which gives much more
stable models and well defined behaviour near the simpler model, see

https://projecteuclid.org/euclid.ss/1491465621

there are a range of those already implemented...

H

parts:
Sorry about the mis-print, the model runs now.

I tried the PC prior, 
PC prior (u=2,p=0.01)
Model hyperparameters:
                                          mean      sd 0.025quant 0.5quant
Precision for the Gaussian observations   5.65   0.963       3.92     5.60
Precision for j                           3.69   1.977       1.12     3.29
Precision for i                         205.57 488.665      17.13    86.87

the results are similar to logtnormal, 
Model hyperparameters:
                                          mean     sd 0.025quant 0.5quant
Precision for the Gaussian observations   5.72   0.98      3.977     5.66
Precision for j                           3.21   1.82      0.887     2.83
Precision for i                         142.33 272.80     14.974    69.32

both are different from the default loggamma prior. 
Model hyperparameters:
                                            mean       sd 0.025quant 0.5quant
Precision for the Gaussian observations     5.18 7.87e-01       3.78     5.13
Precision for j                             4.85 2.56e+00       1.50     4.33
Precision for i                         18355.00 1.81e+04    1228.68 13010.12

Should we use PC instead of loggamma by default for iid models?

Thanks
dong
